title: Three Weeks and One Short Bandage
subtitle: 身体健康 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）
meta: 主题语境：身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）　|　核心词汇：waist　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 waist 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1956 the doctor ① bended the waist that no patient in the clinic would have measured, and he said the bending was the whole of the week. The ② waist, meaning the joint itself and not the bandage, ran three weeks and stayed unmeasured in the book; a waist, he said, is the only thing in a clinic that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ waist in that clinic had the same short bandage beside it, and the ④ waist at the far bed, meaning the scar they kept for the children to cover and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A waist, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the doctor said the measuring is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the waist was the whole of the matter, meaning the grace and not the joint. The ⑥ waist, meaning the grace and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; waist, he said, is either something you bend or the only word that means both a joint and a grace. He said the grace is the part they remember.

By 1961 the ⑦ waist had become a line in a chart, and the chart had become an argument about the short bandage. The ⑧ waist of the whole thing, the doctor wrote in January, was one clinic and three weeks of measuring; waist, he said, is either the scar at the far bed or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ waist I remember is the joint measured in the chart, which closed in 1963 and is still measured as the quietest in the clinic. A ⑩ waist, my mother said in 1965, is the only joint that improves by being measured; every waist, she said, is a grace that has agreed to look like a joint. She said the grace was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 腰（指卫生所里每一段旁边的那一段）
B. n. 腰（指那段腰本身，与窄窄的绷带相对）
C. 固定搭配：bend the waist 弯这一段腰
D. n. 腰（指留给孩子们遮着的那一道）
E. n. 腰之事（抽象总称，指一处卫生所的腰之事）
F. n. 腰（指病历里写到、被测量的那一段）
G. n. 腰、身段（指一件事里人人都疼却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 身段（抽象总称，指人人都疼却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: bended the waist that no patient in the clinic would have measured
The waist, meaning the joint itself and not the bandage
the waist at the far bed
the waist was the whole of the matter

The waist of the whole thing

answers.why: bend the waist 意为“弯这一段腰”，1956 年那位大夫把卫生所里没有一位病人肯测量的一段腰做了一遍。
waist 意为“腰”，指那段腰本身而不是窄窄的绷带，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被测量。
waist 意为“腰”，指卫生所里每一段旁边的那一段，每一段旁边都有同一卷窄窄的绷带。
waist 意为“腰”，指最远那张床边的留给孩子们遮着的那一道，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
waist 意为“腰、身段”，指一件事里人人都疼却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这段身段就是那件事的全部。
waist 意为“身段”，指人人都疼却无人提起的那样东西而不是那段腰，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
waist 意为“腰”，指病历里写到、被测量的那一段，到 1961 年这一段成了病历里的一行。
waist 意为“腰之事”，大夫一月写道，整件事的腰之事是一处卫生所和三个星期的测量。
waist 意为“腰”，我记得的是病历里测量过的那一段，1963 年养好了，至今仍被说成卫生所里最安静的一段。
waist 为抽象总称，母亲 1965 年说，腰是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的腰。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1956 年那位大夫弯了卫生所里没有一位病人肯测量的一段腰，他说这一遍才是那个星期的全部。（bend the waist）
那段腰，指的是那段腰本身而不是窄窄的绷带，经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被测量。（waist）
那处卫生所里每一段腰旁边都有同一卷窄窄的绷带。（waist）
最远那张床边那段腰，指的是他们留给孩子们遮着的那一道，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（waist）
叔叔说这段身段就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那段腰。（waist）
1965 年母亲说，腰是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的腰。（waist）

The waist at the far bed, meaning the scar they kept for the children to cover and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice.
